item.title: Dynamic Treatment Regimes for RA Patients: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
item.description:
Overview A novel application of offline reinforcement learning to optimize sequential treatment decisions for Rheumatoid Arthritis patients.

Problem Motivation Clinicians often rely on a trial-and-error approach to DMARD therapy due to heterogeneous patient responses.

Methodology Modeled the treatment pathway as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and applied Q-learning algorithms to retrospective clinical trial data.

Key Findings The proposed dynamic treatment regime out-performed standard-of-care guidelines in simulated environments by reducing time-to-remission by 22%.
